extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners (and patent practitioners reviewing examiner practice)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for interpreting and examining product-by-process claim limitations during patent prosecution, including when process steps impart structural weight, how to apply 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections, and what evidence is required to overcome rejections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain claim interpretation in Office actions
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarity of claim terms in granted patents is improved when the interpretation of claim terms is explained in Office actions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early explanation of the Examiner’s interpretation will allow the Applicant to clarify the meaning of a term, amend the claim, and/or provide a more effective response to any rejections, thus leading to more efficient prosecution. The prosecution record will provide a map for the public to understand the boundaries of the patent protection and will inform the PTAB and courts as to what the Examiner and Applicant understood the claims to mean.

rubrics_metrics.name: Give claim terms their plain meaning unless inconsistent with the specification
rubrics_metrics.description: Claim terms are given their plain meaning unless it is inconsistent with the specification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Claims must be interpreted in light of the specification without reading limitations from the specification into the claims. (See: MPEP 2111.01)

rubrics_metrics.name: Use Broadest Reasonable Interpretation (BRI) during examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Broadest Reasonable Interpretation (BRI) is always used to interpret claims under examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BRI does not mean broadest possible interpretation. The interpretation of a term must be consistent with the specification and how the term is commonly used in the art. (See: MPEP 2111)

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider every word of a claim; ignore no limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Also, every word in a claim must be considered in judging the patentability of that claim against the prior art.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No limitation, functional or otherwise, can be ignored. (See: MPEP 2143.03)

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and forms of product-by-process claims
rubrics_metrics.description: A product-by-process claim is a claim where an article or at least one element of an article is claimed by reciting the process of making the article or the element of the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A product-by-process claim can be in either independent or dependent form. Claiming the article and then referring back to a previously presented claim reciting a method of making the article is an acceptable way to present a product-by-process claim. (See: MPEP 2173.05(f), MPEP 2113)

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability of product-by-process claims depends on the product's structure, not the method
rubrics_metrics.description: Patentability of product-by-process claims is based on the product itself and does not depend on its method of production—only the structure implied by the steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once a product appearing to be substantially identical is found and a 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejection made, the burden shifts to the Applicant to show an unobvious difference. The use of 35 U.S.C. 102/103 rejections for product-by-process claims has been approved by the courts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination procedure for product-by-process claims
rubrics_metrics.description: How to examine Product-by-Process Claims: (1) determine what structure is implied by the process step; (2) determine if the prior art reasonably appears to be identical with or only slightly different than the claimed product—if so, reject under 35 U.S.C. 102/103; (3) advise the Applicant that the claim is being construed as a product-by-process claim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow MPEP guidance (see: MPEP 2113). Explain the construction and why process steps do or do not impart patentable weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process steps only limit the claim to the extent they imply structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Product-by-process limitations are NOT limited to the manipulations of the recited steps, only the structure implied by the steps.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a recited process step imparts distinctive structural characteristics to the final product. If the step does not change the product's structure, it will not confer patentable weight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not require prior art to disclose same process to reject
rubrics_metrics.description: In order to anticipate or make a 102/103 rejection, a reference need not teach the claimed process if the product/structure in the reference appears identical or substantially similar to the claimed product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the product in the prior art appears identical/substantially identical, the burden shifts to the Applicant to present evidence that the claimed process imparts distinctive structural characteristics resulting in an unobvious difference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant must present factual evidence to overcome a product-by-process rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant could overcome an anticipation rejection by providing evidence that the product-by-process limitation imparts a distinctive structural characteristic to the claimed product.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A statement or argument by counsel is not factual evidence. Evidence must be presented (e.g., data, comparative structure) showing that the process imparts distinctive structural characteristics. If convincing evidence is provided, the rejection must be withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner must state that claim is being construed as product-by-process
rubrics_metrics.description: The Examiner should explain that the claim is a product-by-process claim and why the recited process steps are or are not given patentable weight.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include this explanation in the Office action so the Applicant is informed and can respond appropriately; this practice aids efficient prosecution and creates clear public notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Process recitations that inherently confer structure may limit the claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Some process recitations inherently confer certain structural properties/characteristics to the product (e.g., chain-stitching confers structural properties).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where the process step inherently changes structure, that limitation can be limiting for patentability. Evaluate and require evidence as appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 35 U.S.C. 102/103 against product-by-process claims is appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: If the product/structure of a prior art reference appears substantially identical to the claimed product, rejection under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 is proper even if the prior art uses a different process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court precedent supports applying 102/103 rejections to product-by-process claims; the key is whether the products are identical/substantially identical and whether the Applicant can show an unobvious structural difference imparted by the claimed process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples guide application of principles to varied facts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use case examples (materials essentially free of x metal, foam insoles 'not molded under heat or pressure,' dental appliance overlayer 'formed by fitting,' lost wax casting, chain-stitching textile, synthetic diamond layer formed by dry-chemical etching) to illustrate how to determine whether process recitations limit product-by-process claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples show: (a) where process steps do not change structure and rejection is appropriate; (b) where process steps may impart structural differences requiring evidence to overcome rejection; (c) that the Examiner should explain constructions and bases for rejections in Office actions. See cited MPEP sections for further guidance.
